summary: Oregon Department of Forestry lookout in Wheeler County: fire watch since at least 1936, current tower built 1958-59. Listed as standing; no public access reported.

facts.design: 14x14 L-4 cab on a 40-foot open timber tower

staffing.status: staffed to at least 1964; current staffing not reported

access.note: Firelookout.com says there is no public access. The register names the Oregon Department of Forestry as administrator; the sources read do not say whether visitors may reach the tower.

events.note: Fire detection at the site since at least 1936 (register); a radio set installed on Baldy Mountain near Waterman on August 11, 1936, where forest guard Earl Huff was located (Oregon Lookouts)
Firelookout.com lists a 50-foot wooden tower in 1936; the register and the 1958 report describe a 40-foot tower
District report: the present house was pulled apart by the wind; a new lookout is needed
New tower and cabin started in October 1958 to replace the wind-damaged house; work halted in November with about half done
Register gives construction as 1958-59 for a 14x14 L-4 cab on a 40-foot open timber tower
1959 report: work resumed in April and the structure was in use by the fire season, with minor completion work over the summer; firelookout.com's 1959 entry describes a 54-foot wooden ODF tower
Register: staffed to at least 1964; Oregon Lookouts notes eleven first discoveries that season

corrections.why: The register and the 1958 district report describe a 40-foot tower. 15.2 m (50 ft) matches the 1936 wooden tower firelookout.com describes, not the current structure. Firelookout.com's 54-foot 1959 figure disagrees with both, so the height is flagged for an editor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and 1958 report: 40 feet for the current tower. Firelookout.com: 50 feet in 1936 and 54 feet in 1959. The earlier and later towers may explain the spread, but no source says so directly.

The register gives 1958-59 for construction. The 1958 and 1959 district reports show work started in October 1958, halted in November, and the tower in use for the 1959 fire season. Firelookout.com's 1959 date refers to a 54-foot wooden ODF tower.

notes_for_editor: Do not confuse with the South Baldy Lookout in the Colville and Kaniksu area of Washington (firelookout.com/wa/sbaldy.html; NHLR US register under /wa/). Access rests on one hobby site's 'No public access'; the register names ODF but gives no access rule. Verify with ODF before anyone plans a visit. Height is disputed (40 ft vs 50/54 ft). Firelookout.com's 'Emergency 1970s' note is unclear and not used. No current staffing or condition report was found.
